name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz under attack; Red Sea disrupted
summary: US disables a blockade runner in the Gulf of Oman on 26 Nov; Hormuz traffic impeded and Red Sea disrupted
state: US Central Command said it disabled the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on 26 Nov, at least the 15th vessel disabled since the US blockade began in April, and has redirected 158 ships since July (Al Jazeera). The US–Iran war continues to impede Hormuz traffic (CNBC, 27 Nov), and the Red Sea remains disrupted by Saudi–Houthi fighting. Two chokepoints disrupted keep the Alert.
for_you: Shipping disruption can delay deliveries and raise prices for imported goods and fuel. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO advisories for the region.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded; two chokepoints disrupted = Alert

sources.title: Al Jazeera — US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
CNBC — Two Italians killed in Kuwait drone attack; Trump says Iran war ends 'whenever I want it'

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
